page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4mds_v2 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 42.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, it includes 472 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, while containing no GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core capabilities, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2355.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 4441.77 and a weak bzip3 multi-threaded decompression result. Memory bandwidth tests show average cached read speeds of 344.91 GB/sec, but uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the weak category. Database operations and static web serving throughput perform in the average tier, with Redis SET operations achieving 6.31 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX8-4mds_v2 offers a highly specialized hardware profile, trading off multi-core compute density for massive memory capacity per vCPU. This makes it a qualitative fit for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing but benefit from high single-core clock speeds. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and memory-heavy text processing tasks. It is less suitable for highly parallelized tasks, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, where its multi-core and uncached memory write speeds present performance bottlenecks.

Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers an exceptional memory-to-core ratio with 168.0 GB of RAM (42.0 GB per core) alongside 472 GB of local storage. Performance benchmarks highlight top-tier single-core execution, including strong single-threaded compression and text processing, though multi-core scaling and uncached memory bandwidth remain weak. Lacking GPU acceleration, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that rely on high single-thread performance rather than massive parallelization. It is highly suited for in-memory databases, caching systems, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
